lockup.summary: The company, its directors, executives and holders of nearly all its shares agreed not to sell for 180 days after the prospectus date. The lead underwriters can give written permission to sell sooner.

what: It is a drug developer testing small-molecule medicines for cancer, including lung cancer and blood cancers.
proceeds: It expects about $134.9 million after costs. It plans to spend about $70.0 million on its lung cancer drug, $20.0 million on its blood cancer drug and $15.0 million on its KRAS drug, and the rest on research and general costs.
risks: It is a young drug company with no late-stage trials finished and no products sold, so its future is hard to judge.
It has lost money since it began, expects larger losses ahead, and may never make a profit.
Even after this offering it will need a lot more money, which could dilute owners or force it to cut back its work.
